tagline: Through the Cheat canyon to a town that held its bridges.
intro: WV 72 follows the Cheat River Canyon, and for nearly six miles the river stays close to its primitive state. Apart from Rowlesburg there is little development, and some stretches give the sensation of complete isolation. Pull-offs look out on the canyon, Buckhorn Run Waterfall and the Tray Run Viaduct.

The B&O's bridges over the Cheat and Tray Run made Rowlesburg matter to armies. When the Jones-Imboden Raid reached the town on Sunday morning, April 26, 1863, Union troops and townsmen called out of church held it.

moments.title: Dunkard Bottom
moments.text: The Eckerlin brothers' Brethren community here lasted only a few years; a visitor in 1756 found them sleeping on piles of bearskins and keeping twenty-eight horses.

moments.title: Rowlesburg
moments.text: Named for railroad engineer Thomas Rowles, the former railroad town on the Cheat keeps a downtown historic district.
